method: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from Obesity Canada and the Canadian Association of Bariatric Physicians and Surgeons (Pedersen SD, Manjoo P et al.), CMAJ 197(27):E797 'Pharmacotherapy for obesity management in adults: 2025 clinical practice guideline update' (published 11 August 2025). Every claim is a paraphrase backed by anchors (scripts/anchor.py): verify.py --source re-finds each anchored span in a fresh copy of the source, checks the claim's numbers against it and rejects copying. LICENCE: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (read at Europe PMC fullTextXML <license> element for PMC12350384). The source's words are NOT reproduced here.

claims.claim: **Lifestyle (health behaviour) change alone usually gives only 3%–5% weight loss**, often not kept off and not enough to improve most complications. Medicines are one of the mainstays of treatment, alongside psychological support, bariatric surgery, nutrition therapy and physical activity.
claims.locator: Obesity Canada and the Canadian Association of Bariatric Physicians and Surgeons (Pedersen SD, Manjoo P et al.), CMAJ 197(27):E797, 'Pharmacotherapy for obesity management in adults: 2025 clinical practice guideline update', published 11 August 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12350384/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Always pair obesity medicines with health behaviour change**, including medical nutrition therapy and physical activity, after a full assessment that addresses contributing factors where possible.
claims.locator: Obesity Canada and the Canadian Association of Bariatric Physicians and Surgeons (Pedersen SD, Manjoo P et al.), CMAJ 197(27):E797, 'Pharmacotherapy for obesity management in adults: 2025 clinical practice guideline update', published 11 August 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12350384/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Reduce weight stigma and bias**; care should be patient-centred with shared decision-making.
claims.locator: Obesity Canada and the Canadian Association of Bariatric Physicians and Surgeons (Pedersen SD, Manjoo P et al.), CMAJ 197(27):E797, 'Pharmacotherapy for obesity management in adults: 2025 clinical practice guideline update', published 11 August 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12350384/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **BMI alone is not enough**: it says nothing about body composition or fat distribution. Sex- and ethnicity-specific anthropometric measures should also be used, so people below ethnicity-specific BMI thresholds are not missed.
claims.locator: Obesity Canada and the Canadian Association of Bariatric Physicians and Surgeons (Pedersen SD, Manjoo P et al.), CMAJ 197(27):E797, 'Pharmacotherapy for obesity management in adults: 2025 clinical practice guideline update', published 11 August 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12350384/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Agree goals before starting a medicine**: realistic expectations, benefits and risks. Targets can include cardiometabolic risk, complications, weight maintenance, appetite control and quality of life, not weight alone.
claims.locator: Obesity Canada and the Canadian Association of Bariatric Physicians and Surgeons (Pedersen SD, Manjoo P et al.), CMAJ 197(27):E797, 'Pharmacotherapy for obesity management in adults: 2025 clinical practice guideline update', published 11 August 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12350384/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Semaglutide 2.4 mg weekly** (trial entry BMI ≥ 30, or ≥ 27 with a complication, no diabetes) gave −14.9% weight change at 68 weeks vs −2.4% on placebo. Nausea, vomiting and diarrhoea were common and mostly transient; gallbladder problems and, rarely, pancreatitis occurred.
claims.locator: Obesity Canada and the Canadian Association of Bariatric Physicians and Surgeons (Pedersen SD, Manjoo P et al.), CMAJ 197(27):E797, 'Pharmacotherapy for obesity management in adults: 2025 clinical practice guideline update', published 11 August 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12350384/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Tirzepatide 5, 10 or 15 mg weekly** gave −15.0%, −19.5% and −20.9% at 72 weeks vs −3.1% on placebo; gastrointestinal effects occur mainly during dose escalation.
claims.locator: Obesity Canada and the Canadian Association of Bariatric Physicians and Surgeons (Pedersen SD, Manjoo P et al.), CMAJ 197(27):E797, 'Pharmacotherapy for obesity management in adults: 2025 clinical practice guideline update', published 11 August 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12350384/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Liraglutide 3 mg daily** gave −8.0% vs −2.6% at 56 weeks; **naltrexone 16 mg with bupropion 180 mg, taken twice a day,** gave −6.1% vs −1.3% at 56 weeks, with more stopping for adverse effects (20.1% v. 9.6%).
claims.locator: Obesity Canada and the Canadian Association of Bariatric Physicians and Surgeons (Pedersen SD, Manjoo P et al.), CMAJ 197(27):E797, 'Pharmacotherapy for obesity management in adults: 2025 clinical practice guideline update', published 11 August 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12350384/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Orlistat 120 mg three times daily (the only PBS-listed obesity medicine)** gave a placebo-subtracted change of −2.9% at 1 year in a meta-analysis of 16 trials. Oily stools, faecal urgency and spotting affect 15%–30% and lead some to stop.
claims.locator: Obesity Canada and the Canadian Association of Bariatric Physicians and Surgeons (Pedersen SD, Manjoo P et al.), CMAJ 197(27):E797, 'Pharmacotherapy for obesity management in adults: 2025 clinical practice guideline update', published 11 August 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12350384/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Consider rare monogenic obesity** with onset before age 5 and hyperphagia, parental relatedness, intellectual disability, structural defects or complex endocrine disease; refer to a geneticist. Setmelanotide reduces weight and hunger in these conditions.
claims.locator: Obesity Canada and the Canadian Association of Bariatric Physicians and Surgeons (Pedersen SD, Manjoo P et al.), CMAJ 197(27):E797, 'Pharmacotherapy for obesity management in adults: 2025 clinical practice guideline update', published 11 August 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12350384/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Avoid compounded GLP-1 and GIP–GLP-1 products** not approved by the regulator, because their content, safety, quality and efficacy are uncertain.
claims.locator: Obesity Canada and the Canadian Association of Bariatric Physicians and Surgeons (Pedersen SD, Manjoo P et al.), CMAJ 197(27):E797, 'Pharmacotherapy for obesity management in adults: 2025 clinical practice guideline update', published 11 August 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12350384/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Obesity medicines are long-term treatment.** Trials consistently show weight regain and loss of health benefit when they are stopped, even with continued lifestyle change.
claims.locator: Obesity Canada and the Canadian Association of Bariatric Physicians and Surgeons (Pedersen SD, Manjoo P et al.), CMAJ 197(27):E797, 'Pharmacotherapy for obesity management in adults: 2025 clinical practice guideline update', published 11 August 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12350384/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Stopping semaglutide after a 20-week run-in led to regain of 6.9%**, while continuing gave a further −7.9%; stopping tirzepatide led to regain of 14.0%.
claims.locator: Obesity Canada and the Canadian Association of Bariatric Physicians and Surgeons (Pedersen SD, Manjoo P et al.), CMAJ 197(27):E797, 'Pharmacotherapy for obesity management in adults: 2025 clinical practice guideline update', published 11 August 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12350384/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Medicines also help keep off weight lost through lifestyle change:** liraglutide, orlistat (after a very low-energy diet) and tirzepatide all reduced regain in trials.
claims.locator: Obesity Canada and the Canadian Association of Bariatric Physicians and Surgeons (Pedersen SD, Manjoo P et al.), CMAJ 197(27):E797, 'Pharmacotherapy for obesity management in adults: 2025 clinical practice guideline update', published 11 August 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12350384/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Doses can be tailored**: the treatment goal may be reached below the maximum dose.
claims.locator: Obesity Canada and the Canadian Association of Bariatric Physicians and Surgeons (Pedersen SD, Manjoo P et al.), CMAJ 197(27):E797, 'Pharmacotherapy for obesity management in adults: 2025 clinical practice guideline update', published 11 August 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12350384/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Established cardiovascular disease:** semaglutide 2.4 mg weekly cut major adverse cardiovascular events by 20% (HR 0.80) in people aged 45 or over with BMI ≥ 27 and no diabetes.
claims.locator: Obesity Canada and the Canadian Association of Bariatric Physicians and Surgeons (Pedersen SD, Manjoo P et al.), CMAJ 197(27):E797, 'Pharmacotherapy for obesity management in adults: 2025 clinical practice guideline update', published 11 August 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12350384/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Prediabetes:** liraglutide cut progression to diabetes by 79%, tirzepatide by 93%, and orlistat reduced progression (6.2% vs 9.0% at 208 weeks).
claims.locator: Obesity Canada and the Canadian Association of Bariatric Physicians and Surgeons (Pedersen SD, Manjoo P et al.), CMAJ 197(27):E797, 'Pharmacotherapy for obesity management in adults: 2025 clinical practice guideline update', published 11 August 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12350384/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Type 2 diabetes:** all five recommended medicines improved both weight and glycaemic control in trials.
claims.locator: Obesity Canada and the Canadian Association of Bariatric Physicians and Surgeons (Pedersen SD, Manjoo P et al.), CMAJ 197(27):E797, 'Pharmacotherapy for obesity management in adults: 2025 clinical practice guideline update', published 11 August 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12350384/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, steatohepatitis (MASH), obstructive sleep apnoea and knee osteoarthritis** can also benefit from obesity medicines combined with lifestyle change.
claims.locator: Obesity Canada and the Canadian Association of Bariatric Physicians and Surgeons (Pedersen SD, Manjoo P et al.), CMAJ 197(27):E797, 'Pharmacotherapy for obesity management in adults: 2025 clinical practice guideline update', published 11 August 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12350384/, retrieved 2026-09-23
